name: Array of Thirteen Kills
reason: Source technique 'Thirteen Kills Formation' (also rendered 'Thirteen Killing Formation') was localized as 'Array of Thirteen Kills', keeping the numeric imagery while fitting the Western fantasy register.
description: Richard's signature calligraphic combat array (Eps 257-259), formed from glyph-like 'Kill' characters. When materialized it floods the arena with a palpable wave of murderous pressure. Corresponds to Zhou Dan's Thirteen Kills Formation in the source, which Luo Zheng countered with a Heavenly Devil Phantom.

name: Vengeful Beast
reason: The source's 'Xingtian Beast' (a culture-specific mythic beast name) was localized to the descriptive 'Vengeful Beast' to convey its lingering murderous will without the Chinese allusion.
description: An ancient beast entombed beneath the Celestial Library whose residual will exerts crushing soul pressure on cultivators; resisting it depends on the strength of one's soul (Eps 50-51). Its massive soul body can manifest in dense purple light, and Zane later withstands its pressure unaided in the Hall of Fourth-Tier Attunements (Ep 288).

name: Crystal Talisman
reason: The source's plain 'jade pendant' used in the Blue Cloud Sect entrance test was upgraded to 'Crystal Talisman' to sound more distinctly magical in the Western fantasy setting.
description: An identification talisman worn by candidates during the Skyreach Sect entrance trials (Eps 29-38). It bleeds from green to a deep red the moment a candidate secures their place, as Zane's does when he touches the tablet; in the source, Mo Can likewise recognizes Luo Zheng passed because his jade pendant has turned bright red.

name: Hell Mountain
reason: Source location 'Purgatory Mountain' was localized as 'Hell Mountain', a close register-equivalent name for the sect's forbidding place of confinement.
description: A forbidding site of the Skyreach Sect where Elara Lowell was confined (Eps 308, 350-351, 764). Her imprisonment was framed as punishment but was actually protective secrecy: a powerful lord covets her rare physique, and the sect claims she is in seclusion there. Zane eventually earns the right to bring her out. Corresponds to Purgatory Mountain, where Luo Yan is locked up in the source.

name: Cloudrender
issues: MasterLS note ('Evan's NEW Mythic Weapon, replaces his earlier fragile Mythic Weapon') conflicts with the delivered episodes: in Eps 320-323 Cloudrender has been Evan's sword 'for years', is called a Sacred Weapon granted by Sir Kenneth, and was lost by Evan to Elara in a wager before the duel.
reason: The source's ornate 'Vibrant Falling Petals Sword' was renamed 'Cloudrender', a punchier compound coinage fitting the adaptation's Western fantasy weapon naming.
description: Evan's prized sword, a high-grade blade granted to him by Sir Kenneth of the Skyreach Sect (Eps 320-323). Evan lost it to Elara in a careless wager and must beg to borrow it back for the tournament final, where Zane still disarms him. Likely corresponds to Li Yifeng's Vibrant Falling Petals Sword, which Luo Zheng could not break directly in the aligned source chapters.

name: Ford Stone
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Ford' was chosen as a blunt, solid name for a ruthless clan lord, and the surname 'Stone' renders his house name for House Stone as a consistent family unit (qiu shan's 'shan' means mountain).
description: Lord of House Stone, the second most powerful family in Castermere County (Eps 335-337). He helped Zane's two uncles murder Milo Lowell and seized a huge chunk of House Lowell's property, his men arriving to claim their prize before the blood had dried. When Zane returns for revenge, he severs Ford's and Chuck's right hands in a single stroke, leaving the county's mightiest lords helpless. Corresponds to Qiu Shan, the clan head who killed Luo Xiao and whose right arm Luo Zheng cuts off in the source.

name: Accomplished Sword Intent
reason: The source cultivation grade 'Great Success Sword Intent' (dacheng) was localized as 'Accomplished Sword Intent' to read naturally in English while preserving the tiered mastery system below the Apex of Sword Intent.
description: A level of sword mastery below the Apex of Sword Intent (Eps 355-363, 617). Nineteen-year-old Alistair Mahoney's attainment of it awes the Crimson Sect crowd, but it is immediately overshadowed when Finn and Zane both reveal the Apex of Sword Intent in the same competition; in the source it is the Great Success Sword Intent, a treasure for any second-grade sect yet outclassed by perfect Sword Intent.

name: Twelve Signs
reason: The source's 'Twelve Earthly Branches Formation' references the Chinese zodiacal branches, so it was localized to the culture-neutral 'Formation of the Twelve Signs'.
description: Lennon Anderson's signature cooperative formation (Eps 368-379), sprung by twelve disciples under his command and powering the Scythe of the River-Winds; per the master sheet even early Inner-Core Realm warriors would struggle against it. Corresponds to the Twelve Earthly Branches Formation that Zhao Xiaohua commands with twelve Divine Reflection Realm Cloud Hall disciples in the source.

name: Nine-Headed Dragon
reason: Source term 'Nine-Headed Dragon' was retained unchanged, as the creature name already suits the Western fantasy setting; its 'Blood Soul' was rendered as 'Lifeblood'.
description: A hydra-like beast of the Cloud Road trials (Eps 374-402). Its Lifeblood (the source's Nine-Headed Dragon Blood Soul) is an extremely rare prize that supercharges a cultivator's own life force and can heal grave injuries.

name: Destiny
reason: Generic capitalized concept word, not a single entity: the folded mentions span distinct things (Destiny Stones, the Wheel of Destiny, a book titled 'Destiny', and 'blessed by Destiny' as a figure of speech), each of which belongs to its own entry if tracked at all.

name: Malevolent Cycle of Life and Death
localized_canonical: Malevolent Cycle of Life and Death
reason: The source cultivation method 'Ten Thousand Fiend Karmic Wheel' was renamed 'Malevolent Cycle of Life and Death', trading the Buddhist karma imagery for a Western-readable name that keeps the wheel/cycle motif.
description: A Tier Five cultivation method of the Blood Fiend Emperor, found by Zane in a silver treasure box on the Cloud Road (Eps 378-400). It is tied to Malice and the path of slaughter, granting techniques such as the Exterminating Wheel/Exterminating Cycle, though Zane's low Malice long limits how much of it he can use. Corresponds to the Demon Blood Emperor's ultimate skill, the Ten Thousand Fiend Karmic Wheel, in the source.

name: Cloud School
reason: Source organization 'Cloud Sect' was localized as 'Cloud School' to distinguish it from Cloud Hall while keeping the shared 'Cloud' branding of the institutions in Cloudhaven.
description: A respected institution in Cloudhaven operating under Cloud Hall's banner (Eps 407-721); Cloud Hall itself grew out of the old Cloud School, which expanded by absorbing third-grade houses like the Drews, Shaws, Dillons and Wards. Its internal competition is far fiercer than the Skyreach Sect's. Corresponds to the Cloud Sect, the feeder sect of third-rank aristocratic children in Cloud Sea City where Ning Yudie rose to prominence.

name: Josh
reason: 'Josh' is the adaptation's everyday US given name for the Cobalt Dragon's human persona, deliberately unassuming for an alias the dragon uses among humans.
description: The human counterpart and alias of the Cobalt Dragon (Ep 980). On the dragon's instruction, Zane claims a 'spiritual master named Josh' in the Lower World gave him his divine glyph (Ep 436), and a letter under Josh's name orders the city lord to welcome Zane as Dragon-blooded, a name powerful enough that even Madame Vermillion and the Dragonfall Palace tread carefully (Eps 447-450). Maps to Qinglong, the dragon dwelling in Luo Zheng's mind in the source.

name: Dragonblaze Hall
reason: Source faction 'Flame Dragon Palace' (also rendered 'Fiery Dragon Palace') was localized as 'Dragonblaze Hall', preserving the fire-and-dragon imagery in a compound English name.
description: A Dragon Bloodline power that aggressively courts Zane after his performance at the Dragon Soar Arena (Eps 446-450). Its vice leader Alan Nolan sees landing Zane as a massive feather in his cap, and even its leader comes in person yet fails to tempt him. Corresponds to the Flame Dragon Palace, the Dragon Bloodline human force Zhao Zheng belongs to in the source.

name: Keith
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Keith' was chosen as a plain, sturdy name fitting the straightforward strongman archetype of Hu Tie ('tie' means iron).
description: A burly disciple ranked ninth at Eagle Peak who faces Zane in the peak competition (Eps 81-82). He disdains subtlety, relying on overwhelming raw strength to obliterate any defense, and is stunned when Zane takes his blows head-on at the Marrow Refining Level. Corresponds to Hu Tie, the straightforward Vulture Peak powerhouse in the source.

name: Bishop
issues: Merged surface form: 'Bishop' refers to at least three distinct characters across episode ranges - Bishop Sterling (Ep 99, Paige's master, = source Zhuge Feng), Jared Bishop (Ep 1056, a different fighter), and Alice Bishop (Ep 478, the innkeeper's daughter). The Ep 1056 and Ep 478 mentions must not be counted under Bishop Sterling.
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Bishop Sterling' was coined as an imposing, aristocratic name for the feared young master Zhuge Feng, whose family name alone is meant to end an auction bidding war.
description: A feared young power at the auction arc (Ep 99): Paige invokes 'my master is Bishop Sterling' to scare Zane out of bidding, but Zane defiantly raises his bid anyway. Corresponds to Zhuge Feng of the mighty Zhuge Family, whose name Concubine Zhuo wields the same way at the Tianlu Auction House in the source.

name: Small Heavenly Tribulations
reason: Source term 'Minor Tribulations' was localized as 'Small Heavenly Tribulations', making explicit that these are the lesser grade of heaven-sent tribulations.
description: Lesser heavenly tribulations that warriors weather in the Life-and-Death Realm (Eps 1030-1109); enduring nine of them, as Zane's opponent had, marks exceptional strength, since in the source warriors who reach that realm after only five or six Minor Tribulations are considered the bottom class of the upper world.

name: Hall of Blades
reason: Source location 'Sword Testing Hall' was renamed 'Hall of Blades', a tighter English name for the Mist Palace's weapons-training hall.
description: A great training hall deep within the Mist Palace (Eps 1111-1217) containing dreamlike practice spaces rather than combat arenas. A glowing screen records and ranks every attack on the Argent-Gold Demon Peak against a Soul Realm benchmark, and Zane's sword strike holds its number one spot. Layla walks into it under the eyes of half the palace (Ep 1113). Likely corresponds to the Sword Testing Hall of the Misty Cloud Heavenly Palace in the source.

name: Argus
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Argus' was chosen as a hard-edged classical name for the hulking opponent You Hu.
description: A brutish opponent Zane faces in the Illusion Battlefield arc (Eps 1140-1141) whose body ends up falling straight toward the steel below. Corresponds to You Hu, who rams Luo Zheng with the skull on his shoulder and then stares in despair at the cold-gleaming blade beneath him in the source.

name: Maverick
reason: The source moniker 'Youmeng' (rendered 'Serene Dream'/'Deep Dream' in translation) was replaced with 'Maverick', a swaggering US-style codename matching his showy fighting style.
description: An elite enemy warrior wielding the Infinite Crystal Sword, a divine artifact that splits into an ever-multiplying rain of equally powerful crystal swords (Eps 1176-1250). Corresponds to Youmeng ('Serene Dream'), one of Yao Yao's two most capable Fiend Night Clan subordinates, whose Myriad Life Crystal Sword is ranked 2120 on the Universal Myriad Spirit Stele in the source.

name: Ranell
reason: The source title-name 'Celestial Venerable Profound Demon' was replaced with the invented personal name 'Ranell', since the adaptation renders such beings as named Supreme Lords.
description: A mid-rank Supreme Lord 'of the Ogres' among the powers converging on Zane's treasures (Eps 1183-1189). He arrives trailed by a swarm of vengeful Bone Curse Clan shades, offers to take Zane as a disciple in exchange for the Crown of Destiny and the Elysian Keep, and when refused unleashes a crescent of light whose power sends the surrounding universal energy haywire. Corresponds to Celestial Venerable Profound Demon, whose Heavenly Emperor Divergent Mystic Saber produces exactly such a crescent-moon saber light in the source.

name: Dark and Light Energy
reason: The source's 'yin and yang energies' were localized as 'Dark and Light Energies', replacing the Chinese cosmological pairing with a direct Western equivalent.
description: Paired primordial energies encountered in the late-story battles (Eps 979-1196) that morph into attacking constructs, from strange flowers and thorny vines to the humanoid form of Gus himself. Corresponds to the yin and yang energies that transform into ever more Sacred Race members in the source.

name: Star Essence Iron
reason: Source material 'Star Jade Iron' was localized as 'Star Essence Iron', swapping 'jade' for 'essence' to avoid the Chinese jade motif while keeping the stellar origin.
description: An impossibly heavy metal taken from lightless Dark Stars (Eps 1198-1199): merely placing it on a rune-supported chassis sinks the ground a thousand feet, yet Zane lifts the massive piece like ordinary metal. It is forged into his new sword. Corresponds to the Star Jade Iron sword embryo worked by Lian Shenzi in the source.

name: Heavenly Venerable
reason: Source rank term 'Heavenly Venerable' was retained unchanged, as the title already reads naturally in the Western fantasy register.
description: A rank of immensely powerful beings in the higher realm (Eps 1081-1285). Even they treat certain figures with caution, and Zane's feat of killing Heavenly Venerables more than once with the Elysian Keep while only at the Soul Sea Realm is spoken of with disbelief.

name: Blade of Hallowed Censure
reason: The source's 'Buddha Sun Blade' carries explicit Buddhist imagery, so it was renamed 'Blade of Hallowed Censure' to match The Hallowed Concord, the adaptation's de-Buddhified name for that faction.
description: A short sword of Divine Weapon grade carried by a warrior of The Hallowed Concord in the Illusion Battlefield (Eps 1268-1309). His standing in the Concord is not enough to be granted a Divine Weapon outright; the blade is only his to carry for the Battlefield. Corresponds to the Buddha Sun Blade, the supreme divine artifact wielded by the short Buddhist Dao cultivator in the source.

name: Vanguard One Hundred
reason: The adaptation coined 'Vanguard One Hundred' as a branded name for the top hundred of the source's unnamed Illusory Battlefield points ranking.
description: The elite top-100 of the Illusion Battlefield rankings, watched across the universe (Eps 1031-1318): every member is an Ace Talent of a different clan, more than sixteen Thoughtless Minds warriors hold places, and Cora's entry sets off cheers in the Apeiron Tower. Corresponds to the upper ranks of the Illusory Battlefield's Fantasy-point ranking in the source, where individual warriors hold numbered spots such as 74th.

name: First-Rank Violet-Core Physique
reason: The source's 'first-grade Extreme Purple Yin Body' was localized as 'First-Rank Violet-Core Physique', dropping the yin/yang terminology while keeping the color-graded physique system.
description: The rarest, highest grade of the Violet-Core physique, also called the legendary Black-Violet Physique (Eps 963-1297). Cora possesses it, making her a prize that neither Krista nor her rivals will let go. Corresponds to Xi Youqin's first-grade Extreme Purple Yin Body, a physique so rare that even fourth-grade holders qualify unconditionally for the Myriad Purple Jade Tower in the source.

name: Ernest
issues: Possible merge: in the source, the bald cultivator whom Luo Zheng slaps into the lode and the lode boss Qiu Ren who then demands stones and sends killers are two characters; the episodes fold both roles into Ernest (Ep 1015 offer, Ep 1021 'sent Ernest flying into the mine with a single slap').
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Ernest' was assigned to the mine-boss extortionist Qiu Ren as an ordinary name befitting a petty tyrant among ascenders.
description: A bully who controls a mining lode and extorts newcomers (Eps 1014-1021), offering Zane the choice to hand over every Sovereign Stone and deliver more daily, or die. Zane answers by sending him flying with a single slap, and Ernest's crew spreads the tale. Corresponds to Qiu Ren, the ascender boss of the Spirit Martial Holy Land's lode who demands True Origin Stones and sends his three right-hand men to make Luo Zheng 'disappear'.

name: Tribulation Flower
reason: Source item 'Calamity Flower' was localized as 'Tribulation Flower' to tie it explicitly to the Celestial Tribulations it helps warriors endure.
description: A flower of the Tree of Earth (Ep 875) that aids lower-world warriors: it can help a warrior face up to nine Celestial Tribulations (Ep 1080). Corresponds to the Calamity Flower described in the source as a benefit for lower-world warriors.

name: Palace Lord
reason: Source title 'Palace Lord' was retained unchanged as the institutional title for the rulers of the great palaces.
description: The title borne by the rulers of the great palaces of the Upper Realm, notably within the Thirteen Palaces hierarchy (Eps 741-1096). It designates an office rather than a single person: different Palace Lords appear across the episodes, as when one comes to meet Zane personally (Ep 1040) and another turns toward Yolande (Ep 1100).

name: Harvey
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Harvey' was chosen as a self-important, establishment-sounding name for Yolande's ambitious rival Xu Can.
description: A powerful figure in the Mist Palace arc (Eps 1044-1074), nearly as strong as a World Lord, who brings in his own recruits and schemes for standing; the arc builds to Yolande facing off against him before the whole palace (Ep 1066). Corresponds to Xu Can, who enters the Misty Cloud Heavenly Palace intending to wrest the Palace Master position from Yun Luo in the source.

name: Quarryheart Sect
reason: The source's 'Wutong Sect' (named for the wutong tree) was renamed 'Quarryheart Sect', an invented English sect name evoking the crystal mine that is the basis of its wealth.
description: A wealthy third-grade sect located near a supreme Aether crystal mine (Eps 474-480); its disciples can casually counter-bid a hundred supreme Aether crystals. Corresponds to the Wutong Sect, a third-grade sect adjacent to a True Essence Stone mine and much richer than its peers in the source.

name: Light of Water
reason: The source barrier 'Abundant Water Light' was localized as 'Light of Water', a simpler English name for the water-natured protective barrier.
description: A vast protective barrier of water-light that envelops Cloud Hall (Eps 522-994). Even mighty attacks only burn long, narrow scars across its surface, and ripples of energy flaring over it are enough to leave guards slack-jawed. Corresponds to the Abundant (Water) Light enveloping the Cloud Hall in the source, which took a monstrous slash with only a narrow blade mark.
